marubozu_bull.name: Bullish Marubozu
marubozu_bull.rule: Body ≥ 90% of the total range. Both wicks ≤ 5% of range each. Close above open.
marubozu_bull.means: One side controlled the session from the first minute to the last. Buyers opened at the low and closed at the high without ever giving ground.
marubozu_bull.trap: On a NEPSE counter that hit the +15% circuit, a marubozu is manufactured — price stopped because it was not allowed to move, not because buyers won an argument. Check whether the close equals the circuit price before reading anything into it.

marubozu_bear.name: Bearish Marubozu
marubozu_bear.rule: Body ≥ 90% of the total range. Both wicks ≤ 5% of range each. Close below open.
marubozu_bear.means: Sellers opened at the high and closed at the low. At no point in the day did buyers hold anything back.
marubozu_bear.trap: Same circuit caveat as its bullish twin, and one more: on a thin hydropower counter a marubozu can be a single seller clearing a shallow book. Check the volume against the 20-day average.

doji.name: Doji
doji.rule: Body ≤ 5% of the total range. Wicks on both sides.
doji.means: Open and close finished at essentially the same price. Whatever happened in between, the session settled nothing.
doji.trap: A doji is not a reversal signal. It is the absence of a signal. It becomes meaningful only after an extended trend, where it says the trend has stopped making progress — and only if the next candle confirms.

long_legged_doji.name: Long-legged Doji
long_legged_doji.rule: Body ≤ 5% of range. Both wicks long, each ≥ 30% of the total range.
long_legged_doji.means: Price travelled a long way in both directions and came back to where it started. Maximum disagreement, zero resolution.
long_legged_doji.trap: Beginners read the size of the range as importance. The range is the argument; the body is the verdict. A long-legged doji is a loud argument with no verdict.

dragonfly.name: Dragonfly Doji
dragonfly.rule: Body ≤ 5% of range. Lower wick ≥ 60% of range. Upper wick ≤ 10% of range.
dragonfly.means: Sellers drove price far below the open and buyers returned every rupee of it before the close. The low was rejected outright.
dragonfly.trap: Needs a downtrend behind it and volume beneath it. At the top of an advance the identical silhouette carries the opposite meaning — read the context, not the shape.

gravestone.name: Gravestone Doji
gravestone.rule: Body ≤ 5% of range. Upper wick ≥ 60% of range. Lower wick ≤ 10% of range.
gravestone.means: Buyers pushed price well above the open and lost all of it. Every rupee of the advance was sold into.
gravestone.trap: On NEPSE this frequently marks the day a tip-driven move ran out of new buyers. It is worth more when the volume is high — a gravestone on 400 shares is one nervous seller, not a crowd.

spinning_top.name: Spinning Top
spinning_top.rule: Body between 5% and 30% of range, sitting near the middle. Both wicks visible and roughly comparable.
spinning_top.means: A small net result after a session of pushing in both directions. Neither side finished with anything to show.
spinning_top.trap: These are the most common candle on any chart and carry almost no information alone. Treat a spinning top as punctuation, never as a sentence.

hammer.name: Hammer
hammer.rule: Lower wick ≥ 2× body. Upper wick ≤ 10% of range. Body in the upper third.
hammer.means: Sellers drove price down hard, buyers took it all back before the close.
hammer.trap: Identical in shape to a Hanging Man. The difference is entirely what came before: a Hammer follows a decline, a Hanging Man follows an advance.

inverted_hammer.name: Inverted Hammer
inverted_hammer.rule: Upper wick ≥ 2× body. Lower wick ≤ 10% of range. Body in the lower third. Occurs after a decline.
inverted_hammer.means: After a fall, buyers found enough conviction to run price well above the open. They could not hold it, but the attempt is the information.
inverted_hammer.trap: Weaker than a hammer and requires confirmation the following day. Without a higher close after it, an inverted hammer is just a failed rally.

hanging_man.name: Hanging Man
hanging_man.rule: Lower wick ≥ 2× body. Upper wick ≤ 10% of range. Body in the upper third. Occurs after an advance.
hanging_man.means: Mid-session, sellers were able to break price sharply below the open for the first time in the trend. Buyers repaired it, but the crack showed.
hanging_man.trap: This is the hammer's twin and the single most instructive pair in the course. The candle is drawn identically. Only the preceding trend separates a buy signal from a sell signal — which is why Lesson 9.5 exists.

shooting_star.name: Shooting Star
shooting_star.rule: Upper wick ≥ 2× body. Lower wick ≤ 10% of range. Body in the lower third. Occurs after an advance.
shooting_star.means: Buyers pushed to a new high and were comprehensively sold into. The close near the low says the sellers finished in control.
shooting_star.trap: Requires the advance. The same shape after a decline is an inverted hammer, and it is bullish. Shape without context tells you nothing.

bullish_engulfing.name: Bullish Engulfing
bullish_engulfing.rule: Candle 1 bearish. Candle 2 bullish, and its body fully covers candle 1's body.
bullish_engulfing.means: Sentiment reversed inside a single session and buyers overwhelmed the prior day entirely.
bullish_engulfing.trap: Wicks do not need to be engulfed — only bodies. Beginners reject valid signals over this.

bearish_engulfing.name: Bearish Engulfing
bearish_engulfing.rule: Candle 1 bullish. Candle 2 bearish, and its body fully covers candle 1's body.
bearish_engulfing.means: A day of gains was erased and exceeded in the following session. Everyone who bought on day 1 is now underwater.
bearish_engulfing.trap: Size matters. A bearish engulfing where candle 2 is barely larger than candle 1 is noise; one where candle 2 is twice the size is a genuine change of hands.

bullish_harami.name: Bullish Harami
bullish_harami.rule: Candle 1 a large bearish body. Candle 2 a small body contained entirely within candle 1's body.
bullish_harami.means: The selling stopped. Not reversed — stopped. After a decisive down day, the next session went nowhere, which is itself a change.
bullish_harami.trap: Harami means pregnant in Japanese, and the pattern is about containment, not direction. It signals a pause; it needs a third candle to become a reversal.

bearish_harami.name: Bearish Harami
bearish_harami.rule: Candle 1 a large bullish body. Candle 2 a small body contained entirely within candle 1's body.
bearish_harami.means: The buying stopped. After a strong advance, the market failed to add anything.
bearish_harami.trap: On thin NEPSE counters a harami often means nobody traded, not that anybody decided anything. Check volume before you call it a signal.

harami_cross.name: Harami Cross
harami_cross.rule: Candle 1 a large body. Candle 2 a doji contained entirely within candle 1's body.
harami_cross.means: The stronger form of the harami — the second session settled nothing at all, inside the range of a decisive day.
harami_cross.trap: Direction comes from candle 1 and the trend, not from the doji. A harami cross after a decline is bullish; the identical shape after an advance is bearish.

piercing_line.name: Piercing Line
piercing_line.rule: Candle 1 bearish. Candle 2 opens below candle 1's low, then closes above the midpoint of candle 1's body but below its open.
piercing_line.means: The session opened in panic and finished having recovered more than half of the previous day's loss. The gap down was bought.
piercing_line.trap: The close must clear the 50% line. A close at 40% of the prior body is a failed piercing line, and failures here tend to resolve downward.

dark_cloud_cover.name: Dark Cloud Cover
dark_cloud_cover.rule: Candle 1 bullish. Candle 2 opens above candle 1's high, then closes below the midpoint of candle 1's body but above its open.
dark_cloud_cover.means: The gap up was sold. Everyone who bought the opening enthusiasm finished the day in loss.
dark_cloud_cover.trap: NEPSE gaps are frequently mechanical — book closure and ex-bonus dates create them artificially. Check the corporate action calendar before reading a dark cloud into an ex-bonus gap.

tweezer_top.name: Tweezer Top
tweezer_top.rule: Two consecutive candles with near-identical highs (within 0.3% of each other), the first bullish, the second bearish.
tweezer_top.means: Price reached the same ceiling twice and was refused twice. A resistance level just proved itself.
tweezer_top.trap: Round numbers on NEPSE — Rs. 100, Rs. 500, Rs. 1,000 — manufacture tweezers through pure psychology. That does not make them fake, but it does mean they break easily once crossed.

tweezer_bottom.name: Tweezer Bottom
tweezer_bottom.rule: Two consecutive candles with near-identical lows (within 0.3% of each other), the first bearish, the second bullish.
tweezer_bottom.means: The same floor held twice in two sessions. Buyers defended one specific price and were not tested past it.
tweezer_bottom.trap: Two touches is the minimum for a level and the weakest version of one. A tweezer bottom at a price that has held four times before is worth far more than one at a price nobody has defended.

morning_star.name: Morning Star
morning_star.rule: Candle 1 a long bearish body. Candle 2 a small body, gapped down. Candle 3 bullish, closing above the midpoint of candle 1's body.
morning_star.means: Capitulation, then a pause, then recovery. Three sessions telling one complete story: the sellers exhausted themselves and buyers stepped into the vacuum.
morning_star.trap: The middle candle must be small. If it is a full-sized body, this is not a morning star — it is a downtrend with a bounce, and it is worth much less.

evening_star.name: Evening Star
evening_star.rule: Candle 1 a long bullish body. Candle 2 a small body, gapped up. Candle 3 bearish, closing below the midpoint of candle 1's body.
evening_star.means: Enthusiasm, then hesitation, then abandonment. The final push failed and the sellers took the level back.
evening_star.trap: This is the classic top of a NEPSE retail run. It usually arrives with a volume spike on candle 2 — the last buyers arriving — and lower volume on candle 3, because nobody is left to buy.

three_white_soldiers.name: Three White Soldiers
three_white_soldiers.rule: Three consecutive bullish candles, each with a substantial body, each opening within the previous body and closing above the previous close, with small upper wicks.
three_white_soldiers.means: Sustained, orderly accumulation across three sessions. Not a spike — a march.
three_white_soldiers.trap: If the third candle's body is markedly smaller with a long upper wick, the advance is already tiring, and the pattern has warned you at the same moment it confirmed.

three_black_crows.name: Three Black Crows
three_black_crows.rule: Three consecutive bearish candles, each with a substantial body, each opening within the previous body and closing below the previous close, with small lower wicks.
three_black_crows.means: Three sessions of steady distribution. Every intraday bounce was sold.
three_black_crows.trap: By the time you can see all three, much of the move is behind you. This is a pattern for managing a position you already hold, not for entering a short — which you cannot do on NEPSE anyway.
